notes: Styling system: one hand-written stylesheet (styles.css) with only two custom properties (--page, --ink in :root); no component library, no Tailwind, no token JSON. Markup is static index.html; dashboard.js only toggles the dosing switch. needs-source.json and rate-ease.json were not in the packet, so no source_locations or ease_estimates for other roles' findings were requested; ease is given per finding in each candidate's _ease_of_fix field. Lint already reports MOT-01 (transition: all on .panel, styles.css:122) and MOT-03 (overshooting cubic-bezier on .switch__knob, styles.css:286); not duplicated here (ease 1 each, one declaration). Low-contrast grey #9aa0a6 (.updated styles.css:106, .metric__label styles.css:144) is left to the measured contrast audit; its root cause is the missing muted-text token in finding 1. Viewed one capture (forced-colours screenshot) to confirm finding 4. Bash was denied in this environment, so `uie findings validate` could not be run. No IME surface (no text inputs). lang=en-GB is set. Strengths: a global :focus-visible outline exists (styles.css:45) and is distinct from hover; a prefers-reduced-motion path exists (styles.css:312); the switch is a native button with role=switch and aria-checked, so Space and Enter work, and its status change is announced through role=status.

candidates.title: Colour values are literals instead of roles: only page and ink are tokenised
candidates.description: Colour should come from named role tokens so states and themes stay consistent. styles.css declares only --page and --ink; 33 of 35 colour declarations are hex or rgba literals, including literals that equal --ink (#1c2b22 at lines 34, 46, 93). Root cause: missing roles for surface (#ffffff x3), border (#d5ddd7 x2, #5f6b63 x3), muted text (#3b4a40 x3, #9aa0a6 x2), hover/pressed fills (#dfe7e1 x2, #cfdcd2, #eef2ef), accent (#2f6b3a x2 plus the chart stroke in index.html), shadow (rgba(28,43,34,.12) x2) and three status families (ok/warn/alarm chips and dots use six unrelated greens, ambers and reds).
candidates.impact: Status colours for chips and dots are defined independently, so they may drift apart; forced-colours and contrast fixes have to be made in many places.

locations.snippet: .metric duplicates panel surface, border and shadow

evidence.detail: only --page and --ink declared; uie lint: 2 of 35 colour declarations use tokens (6% < 90%)

candidates.recommendation: Add role tokens (--surface, --border, --text-muted, --accent, --shadow-card, --status-ok/warn/alarm with -bg/-fg pairs) in :root and replace the literals.

_ease_of_fix.note: One file; values already exist, only need naming and substitution.

candidates.title: Spacing values bypass any scale: 0 of 23 on the 4 px grid
candidates.description: Spacing should come from a declared scale. No spacing tokens exist; values such as 6, 7, 9, 10, 13, 15, 18 and 22 px are used ad hoc (topbar gap/padding, h2 margin, layout gap/padding, panel and metric padding, chip padding 1px 3px, table cell 9px 7px, alerts gap 7px).
candidates.impact: Near-equal gaps (7, 9, 10 px) may read as unintended misalignment and make rhythm between panels inconsistent.

evidence.detail: uie lint LAY-01: 0 of 23 spacing values on the scale

candidates.recommendation: Declare a 4 px-based spacing scale as custom properties and snap each value to its nearest step.

candidates.title: Sensor status cells are empty coloured dots with no text or accessible name
candidates.description: Status must be conveyed by more than colour and must be exposed to assistive technology. The Status column renders with no text, title, aria-label or icon shape; the only difference between ok, warn and alarm is background colour.
candidates.impact: Screen-reader users hear an empty Status cell for every sensor, including the reservoir float alarm; users with colour-vision deficiencies may not tell warn from alarm.

evidence.detail: five status spans with no text content or label

candidates.recommendation: Render the status as text (e.g. reuse the chip component: 'OK', 'Warm', 'Alarm') with the dot as decoration, or at minimum add visually hidden text.

_ease_of_fix.note: Markup change in one table; chip styles already exist.

candidates.title: Dosing switch and sensor dots disappear in forced-colours mode
candidates.description: Controls and state indicators must remain visible when the OS forces colours. The switch track and knob, and the status dots, are drawn only with background-color on empty spans; the button has border: 0 and a transparent background. Forced colours removes these backgrounds, so the switch and its on/off state render as nothing, and the Status column is blank.
candidates.impact: High-contrast users may not find the dosing control or know whether automatic dosing is on, and cannot see any sensor status.

evidence.detail: Dosing panel shows the label with no switch; Status column is empty
no border or forced-colors media query; state shown only via background-color and transform

candidates.recommendation: Give the track a 1-2 px border (transparent normally, visible in forced colours) and add @media (forced-colors: active) rules using system colours (ButtonText, Highlight) for track, knob and dots; text status per the previous finding also fixes the dots.

candidates.title: Metric values use a second font family that falls back to a generic sans-serif
candidates.description: Content should use the declared family stack. .metric__value sets font-family: Futura, sans-serif while the body uses Verdana, "DejaVu Sans", sans-serif; Futura is absent on most Windows, Linux and Android systems, so the readings render in an unpredictable generic face with different metrics from the rest of the page.
candidates.impact: Readings may change width and appearance between the operators' devices, and the numerals may not be tabular.
candidates.recommendation: Use the body stack (or a declared display token with a full fallback stack) and font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums for readings.

candidates.title: Dosing switch flips state immediately with no pending or failure state
candidates.description: A control that commands equipment should show a pending state while the command is in flight and revert with an error if it fails. The click handler sets aria-checked and the 'now manual' status text synchronously; there is no request, no busy state, no error path and no revert.
candidates.impact: If wired to a real controller, the screen may report manual dosing while the pumps are still automatic (or the reverse).
candidates.recommendation: Set aria-busy and a 'Switching...' status while the command is sent; confirm or revert the switch on response, with an error message on failure.

_ease_of_fix.note: Needs the command flow and error state, not just styling.

candidates.title: Readings have no stale, offline or error state
candidates.description: A live monitor should indicate when readings are out of date or the feed has failed. The 'Last reading 14:05' time and all values are static markup; dashboard.js states there is no loading, empty or error view, and nothing changes when the data ages.
candidates.impact: Growers may act on old readings without any cue that they are stale.

evidence.detail: searched index.html, styles.css and dashboard.js: no stale/offline/error class, message or handler; no data fetch exists
comment: no loading, empty or error view

candidates.recommendation: Add a stale threshold that restyles the 'Last reading' line as a warning with text, and an error banner when the feed fails.

_ease_of_fix.note: Requires a data-loading path that does not exist yet.

strengths.title: Dosing switch is a native button with role=switch, aria-checked and a role=status announcement

not_assessable: IME handling: no text inputs exist
needs-source and rate-ease items: files absent from packet
